{
  "candidate_rtl": "module mux_large (
    input [7:0] block_a, block_b, block_c, block_d, block_e,
    input [7:0] block_f, block_g, block_h, block_i, block_j,
    input [3:0] sel,
    output reg [7:0] block_out
);
    wire select_a;
    wire select_b, select_c, select_d, select_e;
    wire select_f, select_g, select_h, select_i, select_j;

    assign select_a = (~sel[3] & ~sel[2] & ~sel[1] & ~sel[0])
                    | (sel[3] & (sel[2] | sel[1]));
    assign select_b = (sel == 4'd1);
    assign select_c = (sel == 4'd2);
    assign select_d = (sel == 4'd3);
    assign select_e = (sel == 4'd4);
    assign select_f = (sel == 4'd5);
    assign select_g = (sel == 4'd6);
    assign select_h = (sel == 4'd7);
    assign select_i = (sel == 4'd8);
    assign select_j = (sel == 4'd9);

    always @(*) begin
        block_out = ({8{select_a}} & block_a)
                  | ({8{select_b}} & block_b)
                  | ({8{select_c}} & block_c)
                  | ({8{select_d}} & block_d)
                  | ({8{select_e}} & block_e)
                  | ({8{select_f}} & block_f)
                  | ({8{select_g}} & block_g)
                  | ({8{select_h}} & block_h)
                  | ({8{select_i}} & block_i)
                  | ({8{select_j}} & block_j);
    end
endmodule
",
  "bottleneck": "The supplied critical paths are select-to-output paths with significant decode/fanout buffering and a final combining stage. A possible contributor is the default-block selection logic; the reports do not establish an exact gate-to-RTL correspondence.",
  "rewrite": "Use explicit one-hot data masking and directly minimize block_a's enable. Its enable is true at sel=0 and at sel=10..15, without expressing it as the complement of nine individual selection terms. This exposes a shallow default decoder to synthesis and permits shared decoding for the other nine enables.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Unmeasured hypothesis: simplifying the default decoder may reduce select-to-output depth and buffering relative to the 1.04 ns baseline. ABC may produce similar logic or introduce different fanout costs, so neither a positive timing gain nor minimum achievable arrival is established.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "The design uses ten shared enables and ten masked data terms per output bit. The simplified default decoder may save logic, but enable fanout and mapping-driven sizing can offset that saving. No EDA execution was available: mapped area below 1006.089920 um^2 and zero max-slew/max-capacitance violations are not verified. This candidate is not a certified cap-compliant result.",
  "functional_boundaries": "The module interface is unchanged, with no state, latency, assumptions, or don't-cares. For two-state sel=0, only select_a is asserted; for sel=1..9, only the corresponding select_b..select_j is asserted; for sel=10..15, only select_a is asserted because sel[3] and at least one of sel[2:1] are high. Thus every output bit equals the required input bit for arbitrary data. This is a Boolean correctness argument, not a completed tool proof. The mandatory complete source and mapped equivalence proofs have not been run, and the requested validation requirements therefore remain unsatisfied."
